## p61 A — Key-destruction instruction; first 77?77 label remains unresolved

**Edition context:** September: a key-destruction instruction with a masked label.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-september-key-destruction-order-september-a-key-destruction-instruction-with-a-masked-label"></a>



**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

<a id="source-p61-a"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-radio-september-key-destruction-order-p61-a"></a>

### p61 A

Childs p61, PDF page 64; [source crop](../../experiments/september_radio_instructions/sources/p61_A.png). Unchanged published **Sep19–21** key; native **176** coordinates, matching the printed length.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Source transcription — received header:**

```text
21st SEPTEMBER, 1918.
A) --- v -- (10.09 p.m. September 22nd)
FEER POT COS NR 230 (19 DEN9) 1825 (19)
RIZI--176
```

**Raw output — 80/88 fixed positions; no frame change:**

```text
FUN?AX?OTIXUNDTIFLSSXSCHLUESSEL77?77X77777LI?RS?FOTTZUVETZICHTENXDA?EKANNTXFU??AXOSMANIE
```

**Edited output — 7 observed-coordinate substitutions and 7 printed-mask fills; 87/88 fixed positions:**

```text
FUNKAXPOTIXUNDTIFLISXSCHLUESSEL77?77X77777HIERSOFORTZUVERNICHTENXDABEKANNTXFUNKAXOSMANIE
```

</details>

Observed coordinate changes, with zero-based source indices: **0 G→D**, **25 X→V**, **53 G→X**, **77 G→D**, **83 V→F**, **164 G→X**, **171 X→A**.

Printed-mask fills: **4→D**, **12→G**, **54→D**, **55→D**, **56→G**, **95→D**, **96→D**.

The fixed positions satisfy their exact coordinate pairs. The remaining key-label position stays unresolved; a complete plaintext re-encryption is not claimed.

**Readable German — complete edited stream with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Funka Poti und Tiflis. Schluessel 77?77 77777 hier sofort zu vernichten, da bekannt. Funka Osmanie.

**Meaning:** The proposed message addresses the radio stations at Poti and Tiflis and instructs immediate destruction of the key bearing the labels 77?77 and 77777 because it is known. The two number labels and closing OSMANIE remain literal. HIER and several damaged words are editorial proposals; this does not prove that destruction occurred.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-september-key-destruction-order-what-the-key-number-does-and-does-not-establish"></a>

### Incomplete key number and conditional repeated-number completion

The source masks leave the first key label **77?77** incomplete. The second
label is directly decoded as **77777**. The baseline edited stream preserves
that distinction and the readable German retains the unresolved question
mark. It is not question punctuation.

**Conditional interpretation — repeated-number completion:**

If the two adjacent labels repeat one key number, replacing the first
`77?77` with `77777` requires one additional printed-mask fill:
**source 11 L→D** at the coordinate layer. L is outside ADFGVX, so this is a
mask fill, not a substitution of an observed valid coordinate. The optional
complete stream and its exact re-encryption are kept separately in the
certificate. No reference numeral is silently normalized or counted as a
baseline recovery.

The lexical reading **HIER** repairs raw `LI?R`, and **SOFORT ZU VERNICHTEN**
repairs `S?FOTT ZU VETZICHTEN`. These are explicit editorial proposals with
the costs listed above; another copy has not independently corroborated
them. The final **OSMANIE** stays literal. No modern place-name spelling is
substituted into the plaintext.

The heading 21 September, reception 22 September and internal 19 date fields
are preserved independently. Their difference is not resolved by changing
the ciphertext key or its labels.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-september-key-destruction-order-attribution-and-evidence"></a>

### Attribution and evidence

The unchanged published key retains its original recovery credit. The frozen earlier OCR rows belong to the companion p57 edition; no p61 candidate appeared in those selected caches. The present p61 reading is derived from its checked source image, without claiming that the absence of a cached row establishes historical decipherment priority. This comparison does not establish an external first-decipherment claim.
